articles.title: Manchester City verdict has significant implications for game’s integrity, warns FA
articles.summary: FA has the power to charge club and individuals. It will assess action once appeal process is over. The Football Association has confirmed it has powers to take disciplinary action against Manchester City and key individuals at the club in the governing body’s first comment since City were found…
body: The FA said the independent commission’s decision on City had “significant implications for the integrity of the game” and that it “will take action where appropriate.”

City intend to appeal against the verdict of the commission, who after a 42-hearing concluded the club had used a “Disguised Funding Scheme” and “sham contracts” to boost their income by more than £900m between 2009 and 2018.

The FA will wait until the appeal process has concluded, which based on the Premier League’s rulebook should be by the end of January, before deciding whether to take action but confirmed it was monitoring the case closely.
The FA also has powers to take action against individuals proven to have broken rules and/or acted dishonestly, which the commission concluded had been the case.

articles.title: Kim leads Asian Games seeking military exemption
articles.summary: Tom Kim tops the men's leaderboard after the third round at the Asian Games as he seeks a gold medal that will significantly reduce the time he is required to spend in South Korea's military.
body: Having started two shots off the lead, Kim hit a brilliant five-under 65 that included five birdies and an eagle, taking him a stroke clear at 12 under par with one round to play.
Able-bodied South Korean males are usually required to undertake between 18 and 21 months of military service before the age of 28.
However the government rewards Asian Games gold medals and Olympic medals of any colour with a service exemption bar basic training, which lasts less than a month.
Athletes who have previously secured the exemption include former Tottenham footballer Son Heung-min, who served for only three weeks in 2020 having won the Asian Games two years earlier.

articles.title: Uzbekistan dominates chess Olympiad while England’s Sivanandan, 11, sets new world age record
articles.summary: Host nation won having led almost from start to finish, while young English player reached a stunning landmark. Uzbekistan, the host nation, won the open gold medals at the 2026 Olympiad, the biennial chess international team tournament, at Samarkand last week in the style of the legendary Soviet…
body: The hosts led almost from start to finish, with world No 5 Nodirbek Abdusattorov and the world title challenger Javokhir Sindarov their top-board powerhouses. The team recovered swiftly from a single defeat by Germany, and were particularly impressive in crushing Armenia by 3.5-0.5 in the penultimate round. The Uzbekistan government rewarded each of the five players with $200,000 (£178,000), a house and a Volkswagen, plus $50,000 for the coach Rustam Kasimdzhanov.

India performed in line with their seeding. Putting the world champion, Gukesh Dommaraju, on board four boosted his results but also underlined that Sindarov is the favourite for the coming world championship match. Gukesh was exposed in the final rounds when he was outplayed against both Germany, although he won that game fortuitously, and Hungary.
The final leading scores were: Uzbekistan 20/22 match points; India and Germany 18; USA, Azerbaijan, Armenia and Hungary 17; China, France, Spain, Ukraine and England 16 (206 teams competed).

articles.title: Watson and Browns hold off Steelers’ fightback on last-gasp 56-yard field goal
articles.summary: Szmyt hits career-long kick with 10 seconds remaining. Cleveland improve to 3-1 after surviving Pittsburgh rally. Rodgers throws three TDs but two costly interceptions.
body: Deshaun Watson passed for 268 yards and moved the Browns into position for Andre Szmyt’s career-long 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining, giving Cleveland a 27-24 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday night.
Watson, who completed 24 of 33 passes with a touchdown and an interception, went 4 of 5 for 46 yards as he led a go-ahead drive in the fourth quarter for the third straight week.

The Browns – who are 3-1 for the first time since 2021 – had a 21-7 lead late in the first half before the Steelers rallied to tie it at 24-all. Aaron Rodgers threw a 3-yard touchdown pass to Pat Freiermuth with 1:44 remaining, then sneaked it in for the two-point conversion.

Rodgers, who was 22 of 40 for 299 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions, had one final chance to get the Steelers into field-goal range, but he was picked off by Grant Delpit at the Browns’ 18 with one second left.

articles.title: What does Man City guilty verdict mean for their squad?
articles.summary: BBC Sport looks at how Manchester City's guilty verdict will affect their existing players' futures and the club's dealings in the transfer market.
body: So much has been said about Manchester City since it was revealed they had been found guilty of the majority of the 115 Premier League charges levelled at them.

On Tuesday, it was confirmed that an independent commission found City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the league's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons. The club has repeatedly denied guilt.
Their potential punishment has been debated, the future of the owners questioned and the feelings of the rest of the league - and wider football world - have been aired.
But so far there has been little focus on what it means for one crucial group.

articles.title: 'They'll be hating each other!' - Nelson: Don’t let AJ and Fury smiles fool you!
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury's smiles and respect will be replaced by a boiling rivalry when their fight gets closer, says Sky Sports Boxing's Johnny Nelson.
body: The British heavyweight rivals traded a few taunts but also shared words of mutual respect at their long-awaited first press conference in London on Wednesday evening.

But Sky Sports expert Nelson believes their first media meeting was just a "soft launch" and expects real animosity to appear ahead of their blockbuster battle in Cardiff on December 11, penning his thoughts below...

"I think after all these years of all the back-and-forth and Tyson calling him every name under the sun and AJ being super cool and Eddie Hearn saying what he's saying, I thought when they sat in front of each other on Wednesday, if I'm honest - maybe I got taken away with all the hype - but I thought there was really going to be a real ruckus.
"But they were like a couple of businessmen that went there to say: 'Right, we're going to tick all the boxes.'

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers served humble pie after what he was spotted doing towards Browns fans
articles.summary: Thursday night was another frustrating evening for Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who was dealt his second defeat of the season by the Cleveland Browns.
body: Deshaun Watson set up a late field goal for the Browns to secure the victory in Cleveland, after what was a closely-contested game between the AFC North rivals. Despite scoring the first touchdown of the game, the Steelers found themselves chasing the lead, with a 21-10 deficit at the half.

With less than two minutes on the clock, the Steelers actually regained the lead in the game. However, an Andre Szmyt field goal sealed the win for the Browns in the final seconds, which led to another loss for the inconsistent Steelers.
A moment caught by the broadcast cameras from Rodgers when the Steelers levelled the game has now come back to haunt the veteran quarterback.

Having scored the two-point conversion to level the game with 1:42 left on the game clock, Rodgers was spotted turning around to the Browns fans and pointing to his ear. It would seem he had received some heckling throughout the game, but his gesture came a little too soon.

articles.title: Obrador about leaving Real Madrid for Benfica: “I didn’t think twice about it”
articles.summary: Former Real Madrid player Rafa Obrador has talked to AS about his move to Benfica in the summer of 2025. “When Benfica called me, I didn’t think twice. It was a great opportunity. Every player’s dream is to play in the Champions League, and Benfica always competes in Europe.
body: “Serie A has a very important history, and I think I can adapt well here. Italian football is very physical and intense, but I really like the idea Sassuolo proposes: having possession, playing calmly, and finding spaces. As a full-back, they also ask me to play a bit more centrally, not just as the typical full-back glued to the wing. They want us to be versatile and able to offer various options to the team,” he explained.

Obrador was a quality player for Castilla but was never considered the kind of prospect that could play for Real Madrid in the long term. He will try to earn a spot in Benfica’s 2027-28 team by completing good performances in the Serie A.

articles.title: Verstappen makes fast start in Malaysia to outpace Russell in first practice
articles.summary: ​Max Verstappen made an impressively fast start to Formula 1's return to the Sepang International Circuit to set the pace from George Russell in the first practice session of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
body: With F1 cars back on the popular track on the outskirts of Kuala Lumpur for the first time since 2017, Verstappen - the winner of that last race at Sepang - was quickly back in the groove in his Red Bull and set the pace on a 1:37.520 by three tenths of a second.
Russell, who pipped Verstappen to victory in Baku last week, was second quickest in a Mercedes car that features a major aerodynamic upgrade this weekend.
The package represents Mercedes' first car update of significance since the Canadian Grand Prix at the end of May and includes a new floor, rear suspension and rear corner.

While it will inevitably take a little time for the Silver Arrows to fully assess the revised W17's performance and to get the most out of it, Kimi Antonelli will hope to close up to Russell after the title leader lapped 0.6s slower than his team-mate alone in the first session.
